parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἄνθραξ (ánthrax, “charcoal”), from the accusative singular "τόν (tón) ἄνθρακα (ánthraka); compare dialectal άθρακας (áthrakas, “disease, pestilence”). For the chemical sense, semantic loan from French carbone. For the disease, semantic loan from English anthrax,

Inherited from Ancient Greek ἄστρον (ástron). The figurative sense of "fate" since Mediaeval times. The contemporary terms of the emblem or geometrical shape, semantic loan from French étoile. For "Star Wars", semantic loan from English Star Wars
Learned borrowing from French adrénaline. Suffix -ίνη (-íni, “-ine”).
From Ancient Greek ἀναλύω (“unloose; resolve into its elements”). For modern senses, semantic loan from French analyser and English analyse. Morphologically, from ανα- + λύω.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀναμένω (anaménō, “to wait”), from ἀνα- (ana-) + μένω (ménō), with semantic loan from French s'attendre and Semantic loan from English is expected.
Learnedly from αν- (an-, α- privative) + αποτελεσματικός (apotelesmatikós), a calque of French ineffectif (rare) and English ineffective.
Learnedly from ανασκοπώ (anaskopó) + -ση (-si), a calque of French révision and English review.

parole.termine_origine: rira bien qui rira le dernier

catena.termine: rira bien qui rira le dernier
he who laughs last laughs best

parole.testo: Calque of French rira bien qui rira le dernier or of English he who laughs last laughs best.

parole.significato: to bind (to oblige, restrain, or hold, by authority, law, duty, etc.)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek δεσμεύω (desmeúō) with semantic loan from French lier and English bind.

parole.significato: diaphragm (any of various membranes or sheets of muscle or ligament which separate one cavity from another)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek διάφραγμα (diáphragma) with semantic loan from French diaphragme for non-anatomical technical senses and English diaphragm for the contraceptive device.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek δῠτικός (dŭtikós). Morphologically δύω (dýo) + -τικός (-tikós). In the proper senses, semantic loan from French occidental and English western.
Inherited from Ancient Greek δύναμις (dúnamis). For scientific and modern senses, semantic loan from French puissance or English power.

* For the sense enrol, a learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐγγράφω (engráphō) and the sense enclose geometric shape, from the Hellenistic sense of the word: Koine Greek ἐγγράφω (engráphō). * For the senses record, semantic loan from French inscrire. * For computing, rendering of the English enter
From Koine Greek εγγύη(σις) (engúē(sis)) + -ση (-si), from the Ancient Greek ἐγγύη (engúē). For modern senses, a semantic loan from French garantie and English guaranty.
Learned formation from the perfect participle of εκλεπτύνω (ekleptýno, “to refine”), formed as a calque of French raffiné and calque of English refined.
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ἐναλλακτικός (enallaktikós, “altered”), with semantic loan from French alternatif and English alternative.
Borrowed from French express, from English express, from French exprès.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπενδύω (ependúō) / ἐπενδύνω (ependúnō) with semantic loan from French revêtir and investir and English invest. By surface analysis, επ- (ep-) + ενδύω (endýo).

parole.significato: to survive, to continue to live or exist
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek *ἐπιβι(ῶ) + -ώνω (-óno), the former, of -όω (-óō) conjugation, attested in the aorist form ἐπεβίων (epebíōn, “I continued to live”) of *ἐπιβιόω "to live over", from ἐπι- (epi-) + βιόω (bióō), with semantic loan from French survivre and English survive.

parole.significato: to survive (to live past a life-threatening event)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιζῶ (epizô), contracted form of ἐπιζώω (epizṓō), ἐπιζάω (epizáō, “to survive”), with semantic loan from French survivre and English survive. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + ζω (zo).

parole.significato: fellow (a member of a learned or professional society)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἑταῖρος (hetaîros) with semantic loan from French associé and partenaire and from English partner.

parole.significato: happy (having a feeling arising from a consciousness of well-being or of enjoyment)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek εὐτυχής (eutukhḗs) with semantic loan from French heureux and English happy.

parole.significato: jungle (a large, undeveloped, humid forest, especially in a tropical region, that is home to many wild plants and anima…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French jungle, from English jungle.
Learnedly from ημι- (imi-) + τελικός (telikós), a calque of French demi-finale or English semifinal.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κᾰλῠ́πτω (kălŭ́ptō) and semantic loan from French couvrir or English cover.
The transitive sense inherited from Ancient Greek καπνίζω (kapnízō). By surface analysis, καπνός (kapnós, “smoke”) + -ίζω (-ízo). The sense smoke (cigarette), Calque of French fumer or English smoke.

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek κατανόη(σις) (katanóē(sis), “observation”) + -ση (-si), from κατανοέω (katanoéō) + -σις (-sis), with semantic loan from French compréhension, entendement, as well as semantic loan from English understanding.
Learned borrowing from French clinique and English clinic, from Late Latin clīnicus, from Ancient Greek κλῑνικός (klīnikós).
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek κόμβος (kómbos) with semantic loan from French nœud for 'hub' and 'node' and from English knot in the nautical sense. Doublet of κόμπος (kómpos).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek λίπος (lípos). For sense substance with fat, a semantic loan from French graisse or English fat.
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form. In the noun sense, a semantic loan from French matière grasse and English fat.

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek μονόπλευρος (monópleuros, “with one front”) with semantic loan from French unilatéral and English one-sided. By surface analysis, μονό- (monó-) + -πλευρος (-plevros).
Borrowed from French bikini.
Borrowed from French bifteck, from English beefsteak.

parole.significato: bowl (container used for ornament or storage)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French bol, from English bowl.
Borrowed from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from auto- (relating to cars) + stop (hitchiking).
Learnedly from παραγωγ(ή) (paragog(í)) + -ικός (-ikós), a calque of French productif and déductif and English derivational.
Inherited from Ancient Greek προβάλλω (probállō), with learned semantic loan from French projeter and English project. By surface analysis, προ- (pro-) + βάλλω (vállo).

Learnedly from Koine Greek πρόσγειος (prósgeios, “near the earth”) + -ώνω (-óno), a calque of French atterrir, with semantic loan from English bring down to earth. By surface analysis, προσ- (pros-, “towards”) + γη (gi, “earth”) + -ώνω (-óno).
Learnedly, from Ancient Greek πρόβλημᾰ (próblēmă). For sense "difficulty", semantic loan from French problème or English problem.
From πυρήνας (pyrínas, “kern, nucleus”) + -ικός (-ikós). Calque of French nucléaire and English nuclear.
Borrowed from French shérif plus -ης (-is) ending, from English sheriff.
Borrowed from French smoking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English smoking jacket.
Transliteration of French sport, itself borrowed from English sport.
Borrowed from French stylo (“pen”), which is an abbreviation of stylographe (“pen”), from English stylograph.

parole.significato: compromise (the settlement of differences by arbitration or by consent reached by mutual concessions)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek συμβιβασμός (sumbibasmós, “conciliation, reconciliation”) with semantic loan from French compromis and English compromise. By surface analysis, συμβιβασ- (stem of συμβιβάζω (symvivázo)) + -μός (-mós).
Learned borrowing from Koine Greek συμμόρφωσις (summórphōsis) with semantic loan from French conformité and English conformity. By surface analysis, συμμορφώνω (symmorfóno) + -ση (-si).

parole.significato: somatology (the study of the physical nature of human beings)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French somatologie or English somatology. By surface analysis, σώμα (sóma) + -λογία (-logía).
From τηλ(ε)- (til(e)-, “far, tele-”) + εργασία (ergasía, “job, profession, work”), calque of French télétravail or calque of English teleworking.
Learned borrowing from French téléphonique or English telephonic. By surface analysis, τηλέφων(ο) (tiléfon(o)) + -ικός (-ikós).
Borrowed from French téléphoner or English telephone; by surface analysis, τηλέφωνο (tiléfono) + -ώ (-ó).

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ὑποστηρίζω (hupostērízō), with semantic loan from French soutenir, appuyer, as well as semantic loan from English support. By surface analysis, υπο- (ypo-) + στηρίζω (stirízo).

parole.significato: to accommodate, to put up, to host
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek φιλοξενῶ (philoxenô), contracted form of φιλοξενέω (philoxenéō), with semantic loan from French hospitaliser (in its rare and dated meaning 'to give hospitality') and English host.
From French flipper, from English flip.
From χαρτο- (charto-, “paper”) + νόμισμα (nómisma, “currency”), a calque of French papier-monnaie or English paper money.
From χείλος (cheílos) + υπερωικός (yperoïkós). Calque of French labiovélaire or English labiovelar.
Calque of French choline or calque of English choline. Attested since 1854.
